scenarios.name: deploy-command-viper-precedence
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it binds flags in PersistentPreRunE on the root, sets the env prefix, key replacer and AutomaticEnv, uses ExactArgs(1) and RunE with viper.GetString/GetBool, states the precedence, and checks ConfigFileNotFoundError. A gets most of this right, but it binds flags in a loadConfig helper called from the deploy RunE and not in PersistentPreRunE, and it uses errors.As, which is fine for the missing-config check.

scenarios.name: status-command-with-completion
scenarios.rationale: Both responses match the rubric: Args: cobra.MaximumNArgs(1), Aliases: []string{"st"}, a ValidArgsFunction returning ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp, and installation through the built-in completion command with source <(app completion bash) and app completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_app". Neither writes a custom completion command. A adds extras (validation, macOS paths, a user-directory fallback). B is more concise and reuses a named completeServices function.
